title: Scheduler & Cadences
markdown:
The scheduler is an asyncio task started in the FastAPI lifespan (`openexecutive.scheduler.runner.run_scheduler`). It polls every 30s and reads due rows from `scheduled_actions` (in `episodic_memory.db`). The due query uses `claim_due_actions`, an UPDATE…RETURNING claim, so each row fires at most once per process — this assumes a single scheduler instance per database. Polls are gated on an active company profile via `_company_profile_active()`; before onboarding, due rows stay `pending`.

### Operator pause

A global pause switch (`openexecutive.scheduler.pause`, one row in the `executive_control` table) stops everything the Executive starts on its own. It is the first check of every scheduler tick: while paused the tick does nothing — no alert/watchlist sweep, no claim — so due rows stay `pending` and fire on the first tick after resume. Actions already claimed when the pause lands run to completion; pausing holds work, it never cancels it. The same check gates the Gmail poller (the inbox is left unread) and the workflow resumer (no `wait_for_human` timeouts or resumes, and `apply_resolution` records a reply without kicking the run). Inbound conversations — web chat, Slack, Discord, Telegram, Google Chat — are deliberately not gated. The switch is set from the sidebar, the paused banner or Settings in the UI, or via `POST /executive/pause` / `POST /executive/resume`; each flip writes an `executive_paused` / `executive_resumed` audit row. Any signed-in caller may pause (it only holds work); resuming releases every held action at once, so it is the principal's alone (open only while no principal is on the roster). The state persists across restarts (boot logs a warning while paused) and across client-slot switches. `is_paused()` is read-only: a DB file or table that does not exist yet reads as "running", but a read error on an existing DB reads as "paused" — the brake fails closed, so a storage fault holds work rather than silently releasing it while the UI still shows "paused" (the UI shows "status unknown" when it cannot read the state).

### Liveness heartbeat

Every tick ends by recording when it finished and what it did — `ran`, `paused`, `waiting_for_company`, `rotating`, or `failed` when the tick raised — and `run_scheduler` notes when it started. `scheduler_heartbeat()` returns both; they live in process memory, not the database. Settings → Setup status (`GET /setup/status`) reads them: no start means the task isn't running; no tick five minutes after starting, or none for three poll intervals (at least 90 s), means the loop has stopped; `failed` and `waiting_for_company` get their own light. Liveness is judged before the pause switch, because a paused scheduler still ticks: one that has stopped shows as stopped, where the Resume button wouldn't help. A restart clears the previous run's last tick. Due actions run as their own tasks, so a slow brief never ages the heartbeat.

### Cadence DSL

`openexecutive.departments.cadence` supports, all in UTC:

- `daily@HH:MM`
- `weekly@DOW@HH:MM` or `weekly@DOW-HH:MM` (DOW is a 3-letter day, e.g. `weekly@thu@09:00`)
- `quarterly@DD-HH:MM`

`PATCH /departments/{slug}` rejects a spec that does not parse (bad format, unknown DOW, out-of-range time) with a 422 naming the valid formats, so a typo is caught at save time instead of silently never firing. An empty spec means no cadence.

When a department cadence is due, the runner invokes the `department_check_in` workflow and chains the following occurrence via `cadence.enqueue_next()`. The fire is not passed through the authority gate: the check-in sends nothing (it grades Goals, writes one audit row and a Honcho note), and every action it proposes carries its own `gate_action` verdict in the report. Before creating a run the runner applies a skip rule (`department_check_in.needs_check_in`): the check-in is skipped when the department has no specialist agent, has no Goals, or nothing is new since its Goals were last reviewed — no decision or audit row tagged to the department (the check-in's own review row aside) since the oldest Goal's `last_reviewed_at`, and no Goal edited after it was graded. A Goal never reviewed always runs it. A skip leaves no run in the activity rail, is recorded as `cancelled` with its reason (`skipped: …` in `last_error`) rather than `done` — a done cadence row means "the check-in ran" to the nudge engine — and still chains the next occurrence; so does a check-in that fails once its retries are spent, so one broken department does not fall out of the daily cycle. Chaining is idempotent: while a next occurrence for the department is already pending nothing is added, so a row that chained and then failed to record its outcome never leaves two. Seeded departments start with no Goals, so their daily check-ins cost nothing until someone adds one. Deleting a department cancels its pending `dept_cadence` rows, and `cancel_orphaned_cadences()` sweeps orphans on boot.

User-created (dynamic) workflows can carry the same cadence DSL. A cadence-enabled definition enqueues a `dynamic_workflow` action (`workflows.dynamic_cadence`); when due, the runner runs the stored `DynamicWorkflow`, DMs the artifact to the definition's `cadence_person_id`, and re-chains the next occurrence. Saving/updating/deleting the definition reconciles its pending `dynamic_workflow` rows. A cadence definition may not contain an approval gate — a cron fire has no human to ask — with one exception, the **held-writes** pause: when an action step holds a write to a new target, the runner checkpoints the run (`checkpoint_gate`, the owner is DMed), still marks the row done and re-chains the cadence, and stamps `deliver_to_person_id` on the resume payload so the resumer DMs the artifact to the cadence recipient once the owner answers (or the 48 h timeout skips the held writes). Any other gate is still refused at execution: it calls `workflows.gate.ensure_workflow_event`, which raises on a gate so the run is recorded as failed. It previously ignored the gate and stored a completed run with `"(no artifact)"` as its body, which looked like a success every period.

### Department authority & cancelling

A department-scoped row passes the authority gate (`departments.authority.gate_action`, see Org) before it is dispatched: `auto_execute` dispatches; `propose_only` raises an approval card and marks the row done without dispatching (deferred to the approver's next availability window when they are outside it); `escalate` raises an urgent `[ESCALATION]` card (severity high) straight away — never deferred — and likewise does not dispatch, because approving the card is what sends it. As that card is the action's only trace it always lands: unrouted when there is no approver and no principal, and deduped on the whole action (kind, channel, recipient and intent) rather than the summary's first 60 characters, so another escalation sharing an opening — or the same text for someone else — cannot swallow it. An identical escalation folds into a still-open card and gets a fresh one once that card was handled, and a card that cannot be written retries the row with backoff and, once the retries are spent, marks it `failed` — never `done`. (It used to raise the card *and* dispatch.) A `dept_cadence` row is not gated at all — gating it turned every check-in on a propose-only department (all eight seeded ones) into a one-shot card, and the row never chained its next occurrence. Nudge-engine rows carry no department and bypass the gate.

A `pending` row can be cancelled with `DELETE /scheduled/{id}` — the Pulse page's Cancel; the update only moves a row that is still `pending`, so one the scheduler has just claimed is never overwritten. Cancelling only stops work, so, like pause, any signed-in user may: the route accepts a signed-in caller through the UI proxy (its `x-caller-email`, trusted only alongside the `BACKEND_SHARED_SECRET` `x-api-key`), a matching `X-Admin-Token` (`SCHEDULED_ADMIN_TOKEN`, for scripts), or a loopback caller when no token is set — otherwise 401 (token set) or 503. Each cancel is audited as `scheduled_action_cancelled` with who did it.

### Channel routing & nudges

The delivery channel lives on the `scheduled_actions` row (`channel` / `channel_ref`); the runner dispatches through whichever was set at enqueue time — `telegram`, `slack_dm`, `discord_dm`, `email`, or `__internal__` (workflow steps and heartbeats bypass outbound dispatch). Rows left pending by the removed staff-onboarding kinds drain through that same `__internal__` short-circuit (marked done, no dispatch); the removed talent workflows' *ad-hoc* reminders sat on the principal's real DM channel instead, so a one-shot startup sweep (`memory.episodic.cancel_orphaned_talent_reminders`) cancels them — `ad_hoc`, no department, `pending` or `running`, matching the five generated reminder shapes (outreach, interview coordination, reference checks, onboarding check-in, offer expiry) — and clears the awaiting-reply flag on delivered ones so the nudge engine stops chasing them. The marker row in `app_migrations` is claimed first with `INSERT OR IGNORE` in the same transaction, so concurrent boots cannot double-run or crash. The nudge engine (`scheduler.nudge_engine`, default 15 min) scans stalled `awaiting_human` runs, stale commitments, and idle initiatives, then emits `proactive_nudge` rows routed via `people.channel.prefer_channel_for` — honouring each Person's preferred (last-used) channel and availability windows, deferring those outside their window and skipping those with no reachable channel. Emission is capped per `scope_key` (`NUDGE_MAX_PER_SCOPE`, default 3 delivered nudges) so a parked item is not chased forever.

An idle initiative is chased with its department's head; with no head to resolve — no department (what the episodic extractor stores), an unknown department, or no head set — the principal owns it. That source used to skip every initiative without a head, so in practice it never fired. The principal gets self-addressed wording ("<title>" has not moved since <date> — still active, done, or dropped?). If channel routing cannot reach the principal (no channel configured, or unreachable beyond `NUDGE_MAX_DEFER_DAYS`), the nudge becomes an unrouted Briefing card instead, keyed on the initiative and the ISO week: at most one card per initiative per week, and while one is still unread the scan leaves it alone rather than refreshing it every 15 minutes. The emitted nudge still carries no department, and the usual caps and cooldowns apply. A department-tagged initiative is still skipped while its department's check-in actually ran inside the idle window; a skipped check-in does not count.

The stale-commitment source also chases **open loops** (see Attunement): `scheduled_actions` rows with `kind='open_loop'`, recorded `done` on the `__internal__` channel so the runner never dispatches them, whose `awaiting_response_since` is the loop's *due time*. They are chased as soon as they are overdue — not after `NUDGE_COMMITMENT_STALE_DAYS` — with a check-in intent addressed to the loop's owner (which quotes only the owner's own verbatim words and tells the dispatching turn to treat them as data), through the same `prefer_channel_for` routing, availability windows and outbound guard. Until open loops existed nothing in production set `awaiting_response_since`, so this source had nothing to chase. Each scan first closes loops older than `ATTUNEMENT_LOOP_TTL_DAYS` (21) as `expired`, then marks proactive outreach nobody answered within `ATTUNEMENT_IGNORE_AFTER_HOURS` as `ignored` in the outcome ledger. Ranking uses that ledger: a candidate whose person left their last five resolved nudges of that kind unanswered ranks after all others and waits three times its cooldown; a single answer lifts it. Approving a stalled run (however it's approved) and updating an initiative count as acting on the nudges that chased them. The generic dispatch path tags each send with its source (`_outreach_source`) so the ledger can attribute it.

### Alert lifecycle: expiry sweep and the review heartbeat

Two alert-maintenance jobs live here. The **expiry sweep** is loop-level, not a heartbeat row: `_maybe_sweep_alerts` runs `alerts.lifecycle.expire_stale_alerts` (and, on the same 15-minute throttle, `monitoring.research.watch_policy.sweep` — expiring unreviewed research watch suggestions, auto-disabling research-added watches that proved noisy or dead, and filing one `watchlist_suggestions` nudge when ≥3 suggestions have waited ≥7 days; see External monitoring) once at boot and every 15 minutes at the top of the tick — before the company-profile and rotation gates, so an old backlog expires even before onboarding completes, flipping `unread` alerts past their category TTL to `expired` and auditing `alert_sweep`. Pure DB hygiene, no model call, reversible via `POST /alerts/{id}/reopen`.

The **Executive alert review** is a real heartbeat — kind `alert_review_scan`, `__internal__` channel, bootstrapped idempotently at startup when `ALERT_REVIEW_ENABLED` and chained every `ALERT_REVIEW_INTERVAL_HOURS` (6) with the same crash-resilient run → mark-done → chain shape as `nudge_scan`. `_run_principal_brief` also runs a `pre_brief` pass right before the morning brief (a review failure never blocks the brief). Each pass re-examines open alerts with evidence and, within department authority and the privacy rule, routes, nudges, escalates, drafts, merges or resolves them — see the Today section for the policy. The moves go through the real handlers (`message_person`, `draft_artifact`), so the outbound anti-spam guard applies, and `ALERT_REVIEW_MAX_MOVES_PER_SCAN` bounds side effects per pass.

### Principal briefs

The `principal_brief_morning` / `principal_brief_eod` rows (and the client-rotation digest) are delivered by `_deliver_to_principal`, not through a row channel. The principal's `preferred_channel` (`slack` / `discord` / `telegram` / `email` / `any`) is tried first, then the other chat channels they have an id for (Slack → Discord → Telegram). Email goes through the active MCP gateway and is used only when the preference is `email`, or `any` with no chat channel — so an owner linked by email at setup keeps their Slack delivery without extra email. When no channel can deliver at all (a web-only principal, or email with no gateway), the brief is still generated and stored as a run with its artifact — a web-only principal reads it on the Artifacts page — it is just not delivered, and the next occurrence is chained; see Workflows.

## Client rotation claim pause

The `client_rotation` kind (multi-client practice mode, opt-in via `CLIENT_ROTATION_ENABLED`) adds one loop-level behavior: while a rotation's `.rotation_in_progress` marker exists, the scheduler **skips claiming entirely** for that tick. Rotation switches the live company context between parked clients; claiming during the window would fire the just-activated client's overdue outbound follow-ups from a context nobody is watching. Everything due fires on the first tick after the original client is restored. Stale markers (crash mid-rotation) are reconciled at scheduler startup, and the rotation row is idempotently re-seeded both at boot and after every slot activation (scheduled rows swap with the client). See the Client Companies section for the rotation's full design.

An optional `notion_sync_scan` heartbeat (`NOTION_SYNC_ENABLED`, off by default) incrementally re-indexes Notion pages the workspace integration can see into the isolated `notion_wiki` collection (not COMPANY), reconciles un-shared pages, then chains the next tick.
